text: Agents now start over forty percent of pull requests on GitHub, up from seventeen percent in March. Here's what changed. Developers pushed code seventeen point nine billion times in a year, more than the two years before combined. Commits more than tripled in two years, to thirty four point three billion. GitHub Actions runs one thousand four hundred forty jobs every second. New projects with an agent setup file logged eight times as many commits. More than two hundred twenty five million developers use GitHub, led by the US and India. The Octoverse report is free on the GitHub blog and covers the year to September thirtieth. The catch. GitHub only counts agents it can detect, and volume says nothing about code quality. If someone builds your website, ask who checks the agent's work before it goes live. Send this to the friend who still writes every line by hand.
